title: Winning the Battle of Life (Kurukshetra Within Me) - Part - 5 | Swami Smaranananda Giri

# Winning the Battle of Life: The Kurukshetra Within - Part 5

### Introduction: The Internal Conflict
In our ongoing exploration of the Bhagavad Gita and the teachings of Paramahansa Yogananda, we arrive at the central theme of our existence: the internal battlefield. We call it Kurukshetra. It is not merely a historical field in India; it is the arena of the soul, where the forces of light and shadow, the Kauravas of our lower nature and the Pandavas of our divine aspirations, wage a perpetual war. As we continue this series, we must understand that the victory is not won by external struggle, but by internal alignment with the Guru’s consciousness.

### The Nature of Attachment
Swami Smaranananda emphasizes that the greatest enemy in this battlefield is attachment—'Moha.' Attachment blinds the intellect. When we are attached to the senses, we lose our discriminative faculty, the 'Viveka.' Yogananda used to say that we are like children playing in the mud, refusing to return home to the mansion of the Divine because we have become enamored with our toys.

**Story • The Monk and the Gold Piece**

Story: A monk was walking along a forest path when he saw a piece of gold lying in the dust. He immediately covered it with dirt, thinking, "This will tempt someone who is not yet free." A thief, hiding nearby, saw this and waited for the monk to leave. He ran to the spot, dug up the gold, and was overjoyed. But then he realized the monk was poor and had no use for it. The thief ran after the monk and asked, "Why did you cover the gold?" The monk replied, "Because I saw it as a poison to the soul, and I did not want it to harm the traveler." The thief, struck by the monk's detachment, eventually followed him to find peace.

### The Power of Meditation
Meditation is the master key. Without the stillness of the Kriya practice, we are merely fighting our shadows with our own shadows. We must withdraw the energy from the senses (Pratyahara) and focus it at the Christ Center, the point between the eyebrows. This is the only place where the ego can be transcended. When we sit in the silence, we realize that the 'enemy' is only a vibration of our own past karma. By watching these thoughts without identifying with them, we dissolve the battlefield into the light of the Infinite.

### Living the Teachings
Do not think that the battle is won in a day. It is a slow, methodical process of self-discipline. Every time you choose a noble action over a selfish desire, you are winning a skirmish. Every time you turn your mind toward God when it wants to complain or gossip, you are reclaiming territory in your own soul. The Guru is always present, guiding the chariot of your life. As Arjuna surrendered his reins to Krishna, we must surrender our personal will to the Divine Will.

### Conclusion
Stay steadfast. Do not be discouraged by the intensity of your struggles. The fact that you feel the conflict is a sign that you are on the path. The worldly person does not know they are in a war; the seeker does. Keep your sword of discrimination sharp, your shield of faith strong, and your heart open to the grace of the Masters. Victory is assured for those who persevere.
